title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a smooth complex-analytic curve, meaning a complex manifold of dimension 1. An 'uniformisante' t is a holomorphic function t: X → C with dt nowhere zero, i.e. a local coordinate defined on all of X (an étale map to the affine line E^1(C)).

For two such coordinates t and s, Grothendieck defines the quadratic differential
G(t,s) = (−2 s'''/s' + 3 (s''/s')^2) dt^2 ∈ Γ(X, ω^{⊗2}),
with derivatives taken with respect to t. In modern notation this is G(t,s) = −2 {s,t} dt^2, where {s,t} = s'''/s' − (3/2)(s''/s')^2 is the Schwarzian derivative of s with respect to t.

He records the following properties.
(1) Invariance under s ↦ s+b, s ↦ as (a ≠ 0) and s ↦ 1/s (when s has no zeros). These are exactly the generators of the Möbius group.
(2) The additive cocycle identity G(t,s) + G(s,r) = G(t,r). This is the chain rule for the Schwarzian: {r,t} = {r,s}(ds/dt)^2 + {s,t}.
(3) Compatibility with restriction to open sets, i.e. G is a morphism of sheaves.

From (1) and (3) he extends G to the case where s is an étale map X → P^1(C). Such an s is a meromorphic function with only simple poles that is a local coordinate elsewhere; near the poles one sets G(t,s) = G(t,1/s). He then states full PGL_2-invariance: G(t,(as+b)/(cs+d)) = G(t,s).

The next page completes the symmetric statement. There G(t,t) = 0 and G(t,s) = −G(s,t), and G is a PGL_2 × PGL_2-invariant cocycle on the sheaf P_X of étale maps X → P^1. He announces a converse via the theory of second-order linear ODEs. In effect, P_X/PGL_2 (the sheaf of projective structures) is a torsor under ω_X^{⊗2}.

Purpose: this builds the formal framework of projective structures and the Schwarzian. It serves the questions on the previous page about the uniformizing function μ(t) and its algebraicity: the Fuchsian uniformization of P^1 minus three points or of punctured elliptic curves, uniformizing functions in families, and their relation to Picard–Fuchs equations and the Gauss–Manin connection.
errors: No mathematical errors. The formula is −2 times the standard Schwarzian (a normalization choice), and the cocycle and Möbius-invariance claims are correct.
Minor point: invariance (1c) under s ↦ 1/s needs s nonvanishing, as noted. The extension to étale maps to P^1 tacitly uses that the local definitions near poles glue, which follows from (1c) and (3).

ideas.what: G(t,s) = −2{s,t}dt^2 as a quadratic differential attached to two local coordinates
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative as a section of ω^{⊗2}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange, Kummer, Schwarz (19th c.); geometric form due to Cartan and Gunning

ideas.what: Additive cocycle identity G(t,s)+G(s,r)=G(t,r) together with PGL_2-invariance in both arguments
ideas.modern_name: Chain rule / cocycle property of the Schwarzian

ideas.what: Extension to étale maps X→P^1 and sheaf-theoretic formulation, leading (next page) to: projective structures form a torsor under ω^{⊗2}
ideas.modern_name: Projective structures as an affine space over quadratic differentials; sl_2-opers

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but classical sheaf-theoretic presentation of the Schwarzian derivative and projective structures, known at the time through Gunning's work. The only mildly interesting aspect is the context: it links the Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs project to algebraicity of uniformizing functions in families (an accessory-parameter type question). That question is posed on the previous page and is well known in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Target of G is written Γ(X, ω^{⊗2}) (underlined ω), not Ω^{⊗2}.
'Kerf…'/'[?] (3)' before 'la formation de G(t,s)' should read roughly 'Enfin (3) la formation de G(t,s) commute à la restriction à un ouvert'.
The last bracketed line reads approximately: '(dans le voisinage des pôles de s on pose G(t,s) = G(t,1/s)), et dans cette hypothèse plus générale, (1) devient vraie, et plus généralement…'.
On the next page 'GP(1,C)' should be 'PGL(1,C)' / 'GP(1,C)' meaning PGL_2(C).
